title: Falcon 9 Starlink Group 15-18 (27 V2 Mini Optimized, SLC-4E)

azimuth_deg.derived: launch-plane azimuth tuned to the SpaceX/CelesTrak SupGP inclination 70.004 deg: textbook 180-asin(cos i/cos lat)=155.44 deg; sim runs gave i=70.104 deg at 155.87 and 69.908 deg at 155.74 (di/daz ~1.5), interpolated to 155.80 deg
azimuth_deg.src: https://celestrak.org/NORAD/elements/supplemental/sup-gp.php?FILE=starlink-g15-18&FORMAT=json (CelesTrak SupGP 'STARLINK-G15-18 STACK', DATA_SOURCE SpaceX-SV, pre-launch state vector provided by SpaceX; epoch 2026-10-30T05:05:14.30Z; fetched 2026-10-27 ~8:30a PDT)
azimuth_deg.check: inside hazard corridor: NAVAREA XII 747/26 Hazard Area A (alternate window 300402Z-300827Z OCT covers T0) far edge 29-48N 117-39W / 29-35N 118-12W; same polygon as 737/26 used for 15-16 (far-edge bearings 151.8-157.3 deg, centre 154.56 deg used for the surrogate) https://space-notices.com/notice/nav-warning-NAVAREA%20XII%20747%2F26

payload_kg.note: FITTED within 13.0-21.6 t so the published SECO-1 time delivers the SpaceX-sourced parking orbit; SpaceX does not publish Starlink stack mass

insertion_alt_km.derived: perigee of SECO-1 parking orbit: SECO-1 (T+8:39) at perigee, SES-2 (T+53:07) at apogee per SpaceX sl-15-18 timeline -> coast 2668 s = half period -> a=6599.9 km; r_p = 2a - r_a (r_a = 6378.137+266.2)

apoapsis_alt_km.src: https://celestrak.org/NORAD/elements/supplemental/sup-gp.php?FILE=starlink-g15-18&FORMAT=json (CelesTrak SupGP 'STARLINK-G15-18 STACK', DATA_SOURCE SpaceX-SV, pre-launch state vector provided by SpaceX; epoch 2026-10-30T05:05:14.30Z; fetched 2026-10-27 ~8:30a PDT): deploy orbit 251.1 x 266.2 km (mean elements, above equatorial radius), i 70.004 deg; SES-2 at apogee raises perigee only, so parking apogee = deploy apogee (DERIVED)

target.altitude_reference: equatorial-radius (r - 6378.137 km) for SMA; insertion altitude residual uses geodetic altitude (~3 km difference at insertion latitude, accepted via 1 km-weight)

header_notes: Not flown: LL2 NET 2026-10-30T04:02:00Z (Thu Oct 29 9:02 pm PDT), window to 08:02Z, status Go; Spaceflight Now agrees (window opens 9:02 pm PDT). File continues past SECO-1 through SES-2/SECO-2 to payload deploy (POST-CUTOFF lines).

Published timeline (SpaceX sl-15-18): Max-Q 1:08, MECO 2:26, stage sep 2:29, SES-1 2:36, fairing 2:58, SECO-1 8:39, SES-2 53:07, SECO-2 53:08, deploy 1:01:59. Booster: 18th flight (SpaceX), LL2/prior board B1093; OCISLY.
Target orbit: SpaceX pre-launch state vector (CelesTrak SupGP starlink-g15-18): deploy 251 x 266 km, i 70.004 deg. Deploy epoch 05:05:14Z = T+1:03:14 vs SpaceX page 1:01:59 (75 s, noted).

knots.src: https://github.com/shahar603/Telemetry-Data/tree/master/Iridium%20NEXT%207 (SpaceX webcast telemetry; FAMILY stand-in, not this flight)

cd.assumption: same Cd as the ascent fit (fixed 0.4)

burns.name: SES-2/SECO-2 (MVac restart)

target_perigee_km.src: https://celestrak.org/NORAD/elements/supplemental/sup-gp.php?FILE=starlink-g15-18&FORMAT=json deploy orbit 251.1 x 266.2 km (SpaceX pre-launch state vector)

burns.basis: timing from SpaceX sl-15-18 timeline; thrust solved (throttle unpublished) so the 1 s burn raises perigee to the SpaceX/CelesTrak deploy perigee 251.1 km.

notes: CelesTrak SupGP deploy-state epoch 05:05:14Z = T+3794 s, 75 s after SpaceX's published deploy; SpaceX time used.
Perigee/apogee are osculating (r - 6378.137 km) and will differ by a few km from CelesTrak mean elements.

fitted.method: scipy least_squares (TRF, bounded) vs published knots + target orbit

payload_kg.basis: 27 V2 Mini Optimized: ~575 kg each community-reported (spacex.com.pl) = 15.5 t; MaxQ lists 800 kg each = 21.6 t (upper bound). Mass not published by SpaceX
